MOU by Threats: Iran’s Version of “Peace”

The Swiss technical talks ended the way this whole war has gone: with a neat joint statement stapled over a fistfight. On paper, everyone smiles. In practice, Iran and the US walk away telling completely different stories about the same 80 minutes in a room.

From Tehran’s side, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi sells it as a clean win. The US Office of Foreign Assets Control issues a general license for Iranian oil and petrochemicals. Twelve billion dollars in frozen assets are to be released in two tranches. 

A “safe passage” mechanism is set up in the Strait of Hormuz, a “de‑confliction unit” in Lebanon, and four working groups begin their slow dance on nuclear issues, sanctions, and disputes. This is packaged for domestic consumption as Iran clawing back what was “always its own,” not receiving any gifts.

Then Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, parliament speaker and head of the delegation, tells a very different story. According to him, while they were in session, Trump was threatening Iran’s president, the negotiating team, and the country itself with new strikes. 

Ghalibaf says he told JD Vance that Article 1 of the understanding bans threats and coercion, declared that Iran “will never negotiate under threats,” walked out — and did not come back. 

The Americans, in his version, begged for another meeting; the Iranians refused direct talks and agreed to communicate only via Qatari and Pakistani mediators. Out of that, plus 80 minutes of contact and a dramatic exit, came the “successful” joint communiqué.

The foreign ministry’s spokesman, Esmail Baghaei, lays down Tehran’s red lines in plain language. Nuclear and sanctions talks will only happen within 60 days after the preliminary clauses are implemented. 

The US has already authorized energy sales with full insurance, banking and transport. Iran demands total removal of all sanctions, not cosmetic waivers. Within 30 days of a final agreement, all US forces must leave Iran’s neighborhood, and they are barred from reinforcing in the meantime. 

Missile capabilities are “not on the table” with anyone. And whatever is being unblocked, Iran insists it is simply reclaiming what sanctions stole.

Meanwhile, the choreography around the paper tells its own story. Ghalibaf heads to China to lock in another pole of support. Above the Persian Gulf, five US KC‑135R tankers and two KC‑46A Pegasus aircraft circle — a flying reminder that Washington still intends to supervise implementation with fuel lines and AWACS, not only with signatures. 

Reuters reports Marco Rubio struggling to sell nervous Gulf monarchies on re‑engaging Tehran under this new architecture, torn between cheap oil, fear of Iran, and distrust of Trump’s staying power.

And in Tehran’s studios, a new line is drawn: an IRIB host declares that from now on, chanting “Death to America” or burning US flags is forbidden and will be met with arrests. 

The regime that built its identity on ritualized hatred is suddenly instructing its citizens to mute the chant, not because it loves Washington, but because it has just discovered that “Death to America” doesn’t mix well with billion‑dollar oil waivers and asset releases.

Washington says it is building oversight mechanisms on Iran. Tehran says it is embedding itself deeper into regional security, forcing the US to negotiate around its missiles, its proxies, and its geography. 

Both can claim “success” — but only because neither side is honest enough to admit what they actually signed was not peace, but a temporary trade: dollars and tankers in exchange for 60 days without open war.

🖥 Islamabad MoU became declaration of US defeat: Ghalibaf

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Iran and the United States was not the result of pressure but the outcome of the Iranian nation's resistance and strength, describing it as a “declaration of US defeat.”

Addressing the 20th Conference of the Parliamentary Union of the OIC Member States (PUIC) in Baku, Azerbaijan, Ghalibaf said the agreement demonstrated that dialogue produces results only when the other side abandons attempts to impose its will on a civilized nation and accepts its rights.
​
“The Islamabad MoU was not the result of pressure and coercion, but rather the product of the resistance and strength of the brave Iranian nation, an understanding that showed dialogue reaches a result when the other side refrains from imposing its will on a civilized nation and accepts our rights. For this reason, the Islamabad memorandum turned into a declaration of US defeat,” he said.
​
Ghalibaf told delegates that the summit was taking place after a major act of aggression against the Islamic Republic.
​
“The 40-day imposed war by the United States and the Zionist regime against Iran was a criminal act,” he said.
​
According to the parliament speaker, the war resulted in the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, a number of senior military and political officials, and more than 3,000 Iranian citizens, most of them women and children.
​
More than 30,000 people were injured and industrial, medical, educational, energy and transportation infrastructure, along with thousands of residential and service units, were targeted, he added.
​
Ghalibaf said the steadfastness of Iran’s Armed Forces and the resistance of the Iranian people had imposed heavy costs on the United States and “the fake Israeli regime.”
​
“This resistance, born of faith, caused the enemy to lose hope of achieving its objectives and forced it to surrender both on the battlefield and at the negotiating table,” he said.
​
He argued that the war was not merely a military confrontation but a coordinated effort to alter the region’s strategic balance and impose external will on an independent nation.
​
The planners of the aggression, he went on, believed military pressure, blockade, psychological operations and terrorist actions could force Iran to retreat and reshape regional equations in their favor.
​
“What happened was completely contrary to the calculations of the architects of the war. The Iranian nation showed that the era of imposing one’s will on independent nations has come to an end, and you witnessed how the world admired this perseverance and victory,” he said.
​
Ghalibaf also said that Iran sees the future of the region “not in confrontation, but in interaction; not in elimination, but in coexistence; not in imported security, but in indigenous and shared security.”
​
He said Iran is ready to expand cooperation with all Islamic countries on the basis of mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs, good neighborliness and shared interests, and supports initiatives aimed at creating joint economic, trade, financial, scientific and collective security mechanisms.
​
The speaker also thanked the people and parliament of Azerbaijan and the PUIC secretariat for hosting the conference and facilitating dialogue among representatives of Muslim nations.
​
The 20th PUIC conference is being hosted by Azerbaijan under the theme “Promoting Sustainable and Inclusive Economic Development in OIC Member States through Parliamentary Cooperation.”

📌 Islamabad, IRNA – The interior ministers of Iran and Pakistan have agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in security, counterterrorism, and border affairs.

He stressed that Pakistan remains committed to continuing efforts to help establish peace in the region and to further strengthen ties with its “friendly and brotherly” neighbor, Iran.
​
The two ministers agreed to expand cooperation in key areas including security, counterterrorism, eradication of smuggling, cybersecurity and border management, according to the statement.
